subject: Re: ZenithAI parity and fallback bridge
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@zenithai.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mchen@procureco.com>
Date: 2026-10-31T09:12:00Z
Subject: Initial ask — parity + safe fallback for production

Hi Michael,

Quick one from procurement: ZenithAI is evaluating options to replace our incumbent inference vendor. Pricing is the primary blocker — they offered a 20% blended discount plus a 6-month credit to cover migration egress. Our buying committee asked whether Redwood can offer price parity (not necessarily lower price) plus a technical fallback plan in case the migration hits throughput surprises.

Can you share what a parity + fallback bridge would look like (credits, pilot SLA, and a runbook for rollbacks)? We have a pilot in Jan and need commercial terms by mid-November.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement, ZenithAI

Elena — appreciate the note and congrats on getting the pilot lined up. Short answer: we can design a parity offer plus an operational fallback, but there are three knobs that determine the structure:

1) baseline unit economics (monthly token/embedding volumes and peak QPS)
2) length of the guaranteed credit window (we typically do 3–6 months)
3) what you require for an automatic rollback vs. manual escalation (fully automated traffic switch vs. ops-assisted)

I attached a workbook that maps simple credit math to projected spend. Proposed next steps:
- I’ll loop Laura to validate the commercial side and Connor for the runbook/ops SLA.
- If you can share the incumbent pricing line items (token rate, reserved vs. burst), we’ll give a concrete parity worksheet.

We can also propose a staged fallback: pilot-only 30% safety credit + runbook + optional buyout if SLA misses. If that aligns, I’ll put a draft term sheet on paper.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Thanks Michael — a couple quick clarifications from the buying committee:
- The incumbent is offering a 20% blended discount on list and a one-time 6-month credit to offset migration egress and two months of higher-than-expected usage during cutover.
- We need clarity on what constitutes an SLA miss (p50/p95 latency bands, error budget), and what the escalation timeline looks like. Ops will not accept an offer unless a tested rollback path exists that can be invoked in under 4 hours.

Are you able to outline a concrete fallback SLA in writing and confirm whether the 6-month credit is doable (either as dollar credit or token-rate parity)?

Mark
Director, Vendor Operations, ProcureCo
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@zenithai.com>, Mark Chen <mchen@procureco.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T17:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Zenith parity and fallback bridge

Elena / Mark — looping in final commercial response and operational commitments. Summary below; attached are the draft terms and the runbook we’ll exercise during the pilot.

Commercial proposal (high level):
- Pricing parity: Redwood will match incumbent blended effective unit price for the first 6 months of the pilot period provided ZenithAI commits to a 6-month pilot consume window (no long-term lock).
- Migration credit: we’ll provide a one-time credit equal to estimated egress + 2 weeks of peak delta usage up to $75k. If actual delta is lower, the credit adjusts down (see workbook).
- SLA credit structure: for the pilot only, if p95 latency exceeds agreed threshold by more than 30% for 3 consecutive days, we’ll apply a service credit and open a priority remediation channel.

Operational fallback (tested during pilot):
- We will run a scripted rollback runbook (attached) that switches traffic back to the incumbent within a 3-hour window when invoked by your ops lead. The runbook has been validated in a staging exercise last month and Connor is lead for the drill.
- We will provide a dedicated Slack channel and a 24/7 escalation phone for the pilot cutover window (48 hours around traffic switch).

Next steps:
1) Review attached redwood-draft-terms-zenith.docx and sign off on one of three options: parity-only, parity+credit, or parity+credit+performance buyout.
2) Agree pilot dates and runbook validation slot (Connor: can you propose two windows next week?)

Connor — can you own the runbook drill scheduling? I included the fallback_runbook.pdf and the workbook we already shared.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
